title: Sensor dropout: missing data is never counted as normal
purpose: When sensors stop giving data, the system raises a 'no data' alert, does not count that reading as Normal and does not produce a false alarm either. Three cases: crew-2's pulse sensor gives no data at all (missing), crew-4's SpO2 sensor repeats the old value (stale), the cabin CO2 sensor reports an impossible value (sensor_fault). Meanwhile crew-3's real pulse deviation is not lost: one sensor's dropout must not hide someone else's alert. When data returns, readings go back to Normal.
baseline_note: mean values come from ranges.json vital_karar_parametreleri.baz_cizgi. sd is simulator noise only (assumption; the decision rule does not use sd, it uses a fixed difference). hrv_rmssd and blood pressure are not in ranges.json (assumption).

pp_o2.note: equivalent of PIO2 149 mmHg (middle of normoxia 145–155): 149 × 760/713 mmHg

model.note: ranges.json (PR #16 v1.1) values. Before the failure, life support is regulated (net 0): production covers consumption, removal covers production, cabin values stay constant; only the failing gas moves. Volume 75 m³. Times are aligned with the #14 atmosphere engine in the same model (regulated profile); tests/test_scenarios.py compares the cabin series with the engine.
model.measurement_note: Measurement interval is 5 mission minutes (demo: 0.5 real seconds, time multiplier 600); 3 consecutive measurements = 15 mission minutes.

data_quality_rules.note: Consistent with the rules engine behavior and the contract: the Reading validator (when value=None, status can only be unknown; a reading whose quality is not ok cannot be counted as nominal), Comparator.missing / missing-data evidence (Evidence.threshold null) and AGENTS.md §5 (missing data is never counted as normal). The threshold count (3 consecutive) comes from ranges.json vital_karar_parametreleri.art_arda_olcum.
data_quality_rules.reading_status: Every reading whose quality is not ok (missing, stale, sensor_fault) is unknown from the first measurement; it cannot be nominal.
data_quality_rules.no_data_alert: After 'thresholds.consecutive' (3) consecutive invalid readings, a 'no data' alert is raised at caution level (rule_id missing-<metric>, evidence: Comparator.missing, threshold null). The alert clears when a valid reading arrives. The alert reports the missing data; it does not produce a deviation or limit-exceeded alert (cardiac load, hypoxia, ppco2-limit).
data_quality_rules.sensor_fault_value: The value of a sensor_fault reading does not enter the rules engine or atmosphere.step (it is nulled). Even if the value exceeds the threshold, no critical alert is produced; only a 'no data' alert is raised.
data_quality_rules.recovery: When a valid reading arrives, the reading is evaluated again with the normal rules.

missing-heart_rate.condition: heart_rate reading has been invalid for 3 consecutive measurements (quality not ok or no value)
missing-heart_rate.source: AGENTS.md §5 (missing data is never counted as normal); contract Comparator.missing

missing-spo2.condition: spo2 reading has been invalid for 3 consecutive measurements (quality not ok or no value)
missing-spo2.source: AGENTS.md §5 (missing data is never counted as normal); contract Comparator.missing

missing-pp_co2.condition: pp_co2 reading has been invalid for 3 consecutive measurements (quality not ok or no value)
missing-pp_co2.source: AGENTS.md §5 (missing data is never counted as normal); contract Comparator.missing

events.note: While Katherine rests, her pulse rises from her own baseline of 58 to 80 (+22, threshold +15; margin left against noise sd 2.0): cardiac load Watch. This alert must also appear while crew-2's sensor is down.
Sally's pulse sensor gives no data (value=null).
John's SpO2 sensor repeats its last value (97); there is a value but it is not reliable.
The cabin CO2 sensor reports 12.0 mmHg; since the cabin is ≈2 mmHg this is a physically impossible jump and exceeds the limit (3.0).

expected_alerts.why: While Katherine rests, her pulse is more than 15 above her own baseline (58) (rises to +22; 3 consecutive measurements). This alert is not lost even if another astronaut's sensor is down at the same time.
No data from Sally's pulse sensor for 3 consecutive measurements. Missing data is not counted as Normal.
expected_alerts.recommendation: Check the sensor; until data returns this measurement cannot be used for decisions.

expected_alerts.why: John's SpO2 sensor repeats the old value (stale): no valid reading for 3 consecutive measurements. The old value is not counted as hypoxia evidence.
expected_alerts.recommendation: Check the sensor; until data returns this measurement cannot be used for decisions.

expected_alerts.why: The cabin CO2 sensor has reported sensor_fault for 3 consecutive measurements; the reported value is unreliable and does not enter the limit check.
expected_alerts.recommendation: Check the sensor; until data returns this measurement cannot be used for decisions.

expected_data_status.why: No data ever arrived: the reading is unknown from the first measurement, not counted as Normal. 'No data' alert at the 3rd missing measurement (expected_alerts).
There is a value but the quality is stale: per the contract a reading whose quality is not ok cannot be counted as nominal. 'No data' alert at the 3rd measurement (expected_alerts).
Sensor fault: if the 12.0 mmHg value were evaluated, ppco2-limit (3.0) would produce critical; but the value is unreliable. The cabin reading stays unknown, only a 'no data' alert is raised.

forbidden_alerts.why: No alert for someone without symptoms.

demo_notes: Sally's pulse cell shows 'NO DATA', not green; at the 3rd measurement a 'no data' alert appears. It turns green again when data returns.
Katherine's alert still appears during the sensor dropout: the system does not go blind because of a dropped sensor.
When the cabin CO2 sensor produces nonsense the system does not raise a red alarm; it says 'sensor fault / no data'.

forbidden_rules.why: Missing data is not a deviation alert; no made-up cardiac load caution/critical is produced.
The old value is not counted as hypoxia evidence.
The 12.0 mmHg value from the sensor fault must not produce caution/critical as if it exceeded the cabin CO2 limit.
